# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

A runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. When the
repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>

6|export function resolveBlockScalar(

130|function parseBlockScalarHeader(
131|  { offset, props }: BlockScalar,
132|  strict: boolean,
133|  onError: ComposeErrorHandler
134|) {
135|  /* istanbul ignore if should not happen */
136|  if (props[0].type !== 'block-scalar-header') {
137|    onError(props[0], 'IMPOSSIBLE', 'Block scalar header not found')
138|    return null
139|  }
140|  const { source } = props[0]
141|  const mode = source[0] as '>' | '|'
142|  let indent = 0
143|  let chomp: '' | '-' | '+' = ''
144|  let error = -1
145|  for (let i = 1; i < source.length; ++i) {
146|    const ch = source[i]
147|    if (!chomp && (ch === '-' || ch === '+')) chomp = ch
148|    else {
149|      const n = Number(ch)
150|      if (!indent && n) indent = n
151|      else if (error === -1) error = offset + i
152|    }
153|  }
154|  if (error !== -1)
155|    onError(
156|      error,
157|      'UNEXPECTED_TOKEN',
158|      `Block scalar header includes extra characters: ${source}`
159|    )
160|  let hasSpace = false
161|  let comment = ''
162|  let length = source.length
163|  for (let i = 1; i < props.length; ++i) {
164|    const token = props[i]
165|    switch (token.type) {
166|      case 'space':
167|        hasSpace = true
168|      // fallthrough
169|      case 'newline':
170|        length += token.source.length
171|        break
172|      case 'comment':
173|        if (strict && !hasSpace) {
174|          const message =
175|            'Comments must be separated from other tokens by white space characters'
176|          onError(token, 'MISSING_CHAR', message)
177|        }
178|        length += token.source.length
179|        comment = token.source.substring(1)
180|        break
181|      case 'error':
182|        onError(token, 'UNEXPECTED_TOKEN', token.message)
183|        length += token.source.length
184|        break
185|      /* istanbul ignore next should not happen */
186|      default: {
187|        const message = `Unexpected token in block scalar header: ${token.type}`
188|        onError(token, 'UNEXPECTED_TOKEN', message)
189|        const ts = (token as any).source
190|        if (ts && typeof ts === 'string') length += ts.length
191|      }
192|    }
193|  }
194|  return { mode, indent, chomp, comment, length }
195|}
196|
197|/** @returns Array of lines split up as `[indent, content]` */
198|function splitLines(source: string) {
199|  const split = source.split(/\n( *)/)
200|  const first = split[0]
201|  const m = first.match(/^( *)/)
202|  const line0: [string, string] =
203|    m && m[1] ? [m[1], first.slice(m[1].length)] : ['', first]
204|  const lines = [line0]
205|  for (let i = 1; i < split.length; i += 2) lines.push([split[i], split[i + 1]])
206|  return lines

14|export function resolveFlowScalar(
15|  scalar: FlowScalar,

17|  onError: ComposeErrorHandler

20|  type: Scalar.PLAIN | Scalar.QUOTE_DOUBLE | Scalar.QUOTE_SINGLE | null

70|function plainValue(source: string, onError: FlowScalarErrorHandler) {

11|  if (end) {

13|    let sep = ''

15|      const { source, type } = token
16|      switch (type) {
17|        case 'space':
18|          hasSpace = true
19|          break
20|        case 'comment': {
21|          if (reqSpace && !hasSpace)
22|            onError(
23|              token,
24|              'MISSING_CHAR',
25|              'Comments must be separated from other tokens by white space characters'
26|            )
27|          const cb = source.substring(1) || ' '
28|          if (!comment) comment = cb
29|          else comment += sep + cb
30|          sep = ''
31|          break
32|        }
33|        case 'newline':
34|          if (comment) sep += source
35|          hasSpace = true

13|export interface ComposeContext {

16|  options: Readonly<Required<Omit<ParseOptions, 'lineCounter'>>>

27|const CN = { composeNode, composeEmptyNode }

30|export function composeNode(
31|  ctx: ComposeContext,
32|  token: Token,
33|  props: Props,
34|  onError: ComposeErrorHandler
35|) {
36|  const { spaceBefore, comment, anchor, tag } = props
37|  let node: ParsedNode
38|  switch (token.type) {
39|    case 'alias':
40|      node = composeAlias(ctx, token, onError)
41|      if (anchor || tag)
42|        onError(
43|          token,
44|          'ALIAS_PROPS',
45|          'An alias node must not specify any properties'
46|        )
47|      break
48|    case 'scalar':
49|    case 'single-quoted-scalar':
50|    case 'double-quoted-scalar':
51|    case 'block-scalar':
52|      node = composeScalar(ctx, token, tag, onError)
53|      if (anchor) node.anchor = anchor.source.substring(1)
54|      break
55|    case 'block-map':
56|    case 'block-seq':
57|    case 'flow-collection':
58|      node = composeCollection(CN, ctx, token, tag, onError)

61|    default:

64|  }

66|    onError(anchor, 'BAD_ALIAS', 'Anchor cannot be an empty string')

68|  if (comment) {

88|    source: ''
89|  }

95|  }

102|  { options }: ComposeContext,
103|  { offset, source, end }: FlowScalar,
104|  onError: ComposeErrorHandler
105|) {

107|  if (alias.source === '')
108|    onError(offset, 'BAD_ALIAS', 'Alias cannot be an empty string')

119|  if (re.comment) alias.comment = re.comment

Error tokens report their own message. Added a guard for null/malformed tokens.
- [compose-collection.ts](/Users/rushabhshah/muse_agent_study/yaml__c20a295fd5/repo/src/compose/compose-collection.ts): wrapped `tag.resolve` in try/catch like scalars, reporting `TAG_RESOLVE_FAILED` and returning the collection.
- [resolve-flow-scalar.ts](/Users/rushabhshah/muse_agent_study/yaml__c20a295fd5/repo/src/compose/resolve-flow-scalar.ts): caught `String.fromCodePoint` range errors (e.g. `\U00110000`) as `BAD_DQ_ESCAPE`.
- [directives.ts](/Users/rushabhshah/muse_agent_study/yaml__c20a295fd5/repo/src/doc/directives.ts): caught `decodeURIComponent` failures for tag suffixes, reporting via `onError` and returning null.
